comment: The draft implicitly treats non-structured information as text awaiting structuring (‘machine-processable rather than locked in free text’). Clinical information also exists in interpretive and tacit/narrative states that resist faithful coding; forcing them into structure distorts rather than captures them. These states carry a large share of real clinical decision-making.

public.suggestedRevision: Acknowledge in §1.2.2 and §3.6 the limits of structuring: name the interpretive and narrative states of clinical information as first-class concerns, state that the architecture supports (rather than replaces) their human carriers — the conversation, the handover, the narrative note — and caution against measuring digitisation progress by the elimination of free text.
